clue.text: Spin out, as 192 countries take a covetous look back

parts.note: the United Nations had 192 member states when the puzzle ran, so the countries together are the UN

indicators.note: the covetous look is read back to front, right to left

parts.note: a leer is a lustful or covetous sidelong glance

explanation.surface: A diplomatic manoeuvre is dragged out while the world's nations eye something greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To unreel a line or story is to let it out gradually, as from a reel.

clue.text: It helps make Saudi…

indicators.note: to make is to construct, so these letters are built into a new word

explanation.surface: Something that assists in creating the Saudi state, its sentence trailing on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: USAID is the United States Agency for International Development, which gives foreign aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The agency exists to give assistance to developing countries, so it is something that helps.

clue.text: …chains from ring's elements

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on a sailing ship the chains are fittings that spread the shrouds, part of the ship's ropes and cables
second meaning: the ropes, posts and fittings that make up a boxing or wrestling ring

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from the previous clue to make a sentence, but this clue stands alone; 'from' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a vessel's network of ropes, cables and chains, and also the gear set up to form a boxing ring.

clue.text: Yemen breaking up opponent

indicators.note: breaking up means falling to pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Yemen splitting apart becomes an adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a foe, someone who stands against you.

clue.text: Reps hoot rudely for Jordan, once

indicators.note: the letters are treated roughly and without manners, so they come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Congressmen jeer on behalf of the country of Jordan.
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan here is not the kingdom but Michael Jordan, the retired basketball star; 'once' marks that his playing days are over.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopster is American slang for a basketball player, which Michael Jordan was until he retired.

clue.text: The actual origins of Operation Iraqi Liberty?

definitions.text: The actual origins of Operation Iraqi Liberty?

indicators.note: the origins of words are their first letters

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words spell the answer

explanation.surface: A pointed question about the real motive for the invasion of Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: Operation Iraqi Freedom was the 2003 invasion; the setter swaps in Liberty so the initials spell the resource many said was the true reason for the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics argued petroleum, not freedom, was the real cause of the war, so the clue names the motive as well as building it.

clue.text: Palestine suffering punishments…

indicators.note: suffering means being in a bad state, so the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Palestine endures penalties, the thought continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalties are sanctions imposed for breaking a rule or law.

clue.text: …from violent settler frame

indicators.note: something treated violently is knocked about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, the punishments come from a violent settler in a frame-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a supporting framework of a horizontal beam on splayed legs.

clue.text: Republican man concealing deception on the rise — and on the rise again

indicators.note: one piece hides another inside it
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: A Republican hiding a growing scam is making a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rise' appears twice: first it reverses the trick, then 'again' turns it into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent means rising or reviving after a decline, gaining strength anew.

clue.text: Fisherman's rage when taking Lebanon's premier hostage

indicators.note: taking someone hostage means holding them captive inside, so one piece goes within the other
completes the phrase taking hostage: the captive letter is held inside

parts.note: anger is a synonym of rage

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of the country is used

explanation.surface: A furious fisherman seizes the Lebanese prime minister as a hostage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' tempts as a prime minister being kidnapped; it only picks the first letter of Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is someone who fishes with a rod and line.

clue.text: Libels leaderless residents of Comoros, say

indicators.note: having no leader means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the Comoros are an island nation in the Indian Ocean, so its people are an example of islanders

explanation.surface: Defamatory attacks are made on the headless population of the Comoros.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for making false, damaging statements about someone; slander is spoken, libel written.

clue.text: Rig up a single Jerusalem artichoke

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Assemble one lone vegetable, the Jerusalem artichoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Girasole is an older name for the Jerusalem artichoke, a sunflower with an edible tuber.

clue.text: Djibouti's opening lofty type of farm

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: airy can mean high up and exposed, like a lofty room

explanation.surface: Djibouti's first venture is an upland style of agriculture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy farm keeps cows for milk; it is one kind of farm, as are arable and poultry farms.

clue.text: Arab chief invested in offense or protective layer

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or install, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an insult is an offense, spelt here the American way

indicators.note: the chief letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: An Arab leader is cloaked in either an outrage or a defensive covering.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulator is a material that shields against heat, sound or electricity, often applied as a lining.

clue.text: Unstable Emirates getting hotter

indicators.note: unstable means not settled, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: The United Arab Emirates are becoming volatile as temperatures rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamier means more humid and warm, as hot weather is.

clue.text: Symbols of power upset Algeria

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The emblems of authority overturned the state of Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the crown, sceptre and other emblems of royalty or office.

clue.text: Called for more supplies, like Yasir's letters in Syria

definitions.meaning: first meaning: placed a fresh request for stock
second meaning: Syria uses the letters of Yasir in a new sequence

explanation.walkthrough: Yasir points to Yasser Arafat, but only the name's letters matter: they are rearranged to give Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both requesting a fresh delivery of stock and having letters put in a different sequence.

clue.text: Kuwait and Somalia, for instance, top Europe at first in spectacular victory

parts.note: countries are lands, and these two are examples
a lid is the top of a container

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Two Arab states triumph overwhelmingly by beating Europe at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an overwhelming win, especially by a huge margin in an election.

clue.text: Record niece shattered, blurring the sexes

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: smashed to pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A disc smashed by a young relative leaves gender distinctions unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having characteristics of both sexes or neither, so it is androgynous.

clue.text: Florida city's gold to secure Morocco, at last

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to land something is to secure it, as in landing a deal

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Florida town's treasury is used to win over Morocco eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after city stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a major city in central Florida, known for its theme parks.

clue.text: Oman, PLO skewered in satire

indicators.note: skewered means run through and twisted, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Oman and the Palestine Liberation Organisation are mercilessly mocked in a satirical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a piece of writing that ridicules its target, a form of satire.

clue.text: Need to assume Noah's craft returned for rodent

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so one word takes another into its middle

parts.note: must as a noun is a necessity, something you need

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Noah built the ark to survive the Flood

explanation.surface: A rodent must take on board Noah's vessel, which has come back.
explanation.definitionFit: The muskrat is a large North American water rodent valued for its fur.

clue.text: Airmen flying to Tunisia's capital for clothing

indicators.note: flying here means scattered in the air, so these letters are rearranged
a capital letter heads a word, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Pilots travel to Tunis to buy garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tunisia's capital' looks like the city of Tunis; it only gives the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: A crazy retrospective: stage located in a Middle Eastern capital — like the 2008 summit of the Arab League (all of whose members are here)

definitions.text: located in a Middle Eastern capital — like the 2008 summit of the Arab League (all of whose members are here)

indicators.note: looking backwards, so the preceding words are read in reverse

parts.note: mad is a synonym of crazy
a scene is a stage or setting where action happens

explanation.surface: A mad look back at the stage set for an Arab summit in a Middle Eastern capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2008 Arab League summit was held in Damascus, the Syrian capital; the bracket notes that every member state is named somewhere in the puzzle's clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene is the adjective for things of or from Damascus, the capital of Syria.

clue.text: First portion in Bahrain: cod with flashy trimmings

indicators.note: the first portion of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A Bahraini starter of cod is served with showy garnishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bling is slang for showy jewellery and ostentatious adornment.

clue.text: Roll all over Libya

indicators.note: all over means scattered everywhere, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tank rumbles across the whole of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: A bialy is a flat bread roll with an onion-filled hollow, from Jewish baking.

clue.text: Egypt in turmoil, like the sun

indicators.note: in turmoil means in a confused state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Egypt in upheaval, blazing like the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers classify the sun as a G-type main-sequence star, a yellow dwarf.

clue.text: Shockingly, go in for second slates, e.g.

indicators.note: something done shockingly is done in a disturbed, upset way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: It seems scandalous to put yourself forward a second time when critics are already panning you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slates' looks like a verb meaning criticises harshly; here it is the noun, the stone tiles on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Slates are one example of roofing materials, used to cover a building's top.

clue.text: Hoisting flag is what we need, in huge amounts

definitions.text: what we need, in huge amounts

indicators.note: in a down clue hoisting means lifting upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to flag is to tire or droop, to sag

explanation.surface: Raising a banner is what we need, in great numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner being raised, but it is the verb meaning droop.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas is a fuel consumed in enormous quantities, which ties to the oil-rich theme.

clue.text: In Qatar, are lyricists found? Seldom

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the run of words that follows
says the answer can be located within those words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Qatar, all of are and the start of lyricists

explanation.surface: A question about whether songwriters exist in Qatar, answered: hardly ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely and seldom are both adverbs meaning not often.

clue.text: Flexible Sudanese ballerina

indicators.note: flexible means able to bend into new shapes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supple dancer from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseuse is the French-derived term for a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Bush's backing up in Israel — try Mauritania

indicators.note: backing up means going in reverse, so the hidden letters are read right to left
the answer is concealed inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Israel through try into the start of Mauritania

explanation.surface: President Bush's support is wavering in Israel, so he turns to Mauritania instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Bush stands for is. Bush looks like the former US president, but it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.
